utterances.text: That contains a number of tabs; as a matter of fact, eight different tabs.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, right now I have to count. There's no tab whatsoever on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: But is there a first page on this document which refers to numbers from 1 to 8 Bravo and actually refers to 10 cases?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It looks like, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: This is the first --

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: The first page.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first page, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And you look at inside the first case and confirm that this is indeed a criminal report addressed to the district military prosecutor's office on the 23rd of March, 1993?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have -- I have to search now, because what I have here on the first page --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: The first report.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not what you're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me try to find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: This is dated 23 March 1993.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now I've got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Can you confirm, General, that this is a report based on the second paragraph, starting with the word "because," that this is a report because there is a suspected homicide which had been committed?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I will leave this document aside due to time constraints and ask you, General, to move back to the first binder that you have been given and to look at the first tab.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I would ask you to look at the title of the first tab, where it is mentioned, "Measures taken by Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina 3rd Corps and its subordinate units in relation to training."

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And to look at the first document which is in this package dated 10 July 1992.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Would you confirm that this is an order, albeit before the time of General Hadzihasanovic, to form a training centre in Zenica for the training of recruits?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Can you confirm on the basis of the documents that you have received that at that time the state of war was already in force and that there was already going a conflict at that time in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Due to lack of time, I will simply ask you to refer back to the first page, General, and to simply look at the title of the documents, including -- included under this -- under the heading title and to look at the -- the date referring to these documents.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: In July 1992, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And then, if we go down, to look at the title of all documents, 5 December 1992 with the seminar on intelligence; 8 January 1993, "Formation with lawyers"; 24th January,1993, "Training centre for recruits"; 3 March 1993, "Information on how to carry training"; 16 March, 1993, "Training of medical orderlies"; 3 April, "Preparation for upcoming combat operations." And if we would like at this document, it would speak about training. And then, "Technical training" on 12 April "for crews of armoured vehicles"; and then, "Further training for recruits" on the 26th of April, 11th of September; and also, "training of commanders" of the 7th of October. Without having had the benefit of looking at all these documents, would you say that what I've just shown you is information that you did not possess with respect to efforts made to train the people, despite the adverse conditions in which General Hadzihasanovic operated?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is true. I didn't have this material. But I also wrote in my statement that it became obvious that they tried to train. And as I said yesterday, there are pauses in the operations which have to be used for this kind of training. So I think this was the proper way to do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: If I ask, please, to turn to tab number 3, under the heading, "Investigation and inspection." And I would simply ask you, General, to look at the third document which is referred to on the first page and to read the title of this document.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Report on the commission for establishing factual situation in the villages of Susanj and Ovnak." Is this the one?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Yes, General. Is that, on the basis of the documents you have been shown by the Prosecution, does that refer to a factual situation that you have been made aware of in the documents; whereas, there was an investigation in Susanj concerning the death of a number of people and that a commission was established to find out what had happened?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I would ask you - and this will be the last document I will show you today - simply to go to this specific document, which is the last one under this heading, and to glance through this document, and if you can tell me basically what this document is about, or you understanding of this document. It's a document dated 15th of June, 1993, and it is a document which is addressed by the 3rd Corps Command to the commander of 3 Corps as well as to Supreme Command headquarters of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina at the forward command post in Zenica. The report is also addressed to the president of the district military court in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if I read this -- if I scan it and don't read it, it seems that some 90-plus people have been killed in two villages and a commission was established for investigating what happened there, a commission in the way you just described it before this morning, in order to -- to get more light into that case. I think this is the shortest way I can put it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And would that be the result of the case -- the result of the investigation?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would never be the result of the investigation. This is the first step to start an investigation, to find out what happened, and then more steps would follow based on the results of this investigation -- of the outcome of this investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I'm not sure you have the right document, but I believe that this was the result of the investigation. If you look at the last line of the document.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: That the two first paragraphs establish how the order was given and by whom, and then it says that: "After the order was received, what the commission actually established."

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. I wasn't that far yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I perfectly understand, General, because it's a three-page document and it's not easy for you to be given these long documents to look at. But could you conclude that this would be a thorough process, whereas an incident takes place, a commission is appointed, the commission does its work, and following the work of the commission it issues a report which is not -- which is sent to all those interested; meaning the commander of the 3rd Corps, the Supreme Command headquarters, and the president of the military district court, and that in this specific case this was the end of the procedures because no fault could be found?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. I think this is the way I would expect the things to be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I must stop here, General, because of time, and I promised the President of the Trial Chamber I would not go over my time. I thank you very much for answering my questions. What I would like to do tomorrow is we'll have a couple of documents to show you with this, but then we will move on with the procedure that I believe the Presiding Judge will explain to you.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That completes my cross-examination for today, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What we said a moment ago is that the documents, Mr. Bourgon, must be given to the witness straight away for him to be able to have them at his disposal for the rest of the afternoon and the evening so as to be able to respond to your questions tomorrow, and also the questions that you intend to put to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, with your permission, I can give the witness one document straight away. I told you a moment ago that I had two, but the second one has certain errors, so I can't produce it and give it to the witness. What I intend to do is to promise to give these documents about 4.30, to have four sets of documents ready and the four questions, and I can give them to the Prosecution, to the Judges, and to the Victims and Witnesses Unit, which -- so that the witness can look through them this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So provide those documents before 4.30. The Victims and Witnesses Department will have a copy. General Reinhardt, you have followed what has been said. There are documents which you need to have, but I'm afraid they can only give you one now; is that right? So you're going to receive one document now. The rest of the documents will be made available to you in the Victims and Witness Unit of this Tribunal as of 4.30. So if you could drop in and pick up those documents, because you will need them to look at them this afternoon and the evening, because the Defence intends to ask you questions about those documents tomorrow. Would it be inconvenient for you to come and pick up those documents at 4.30 this afternoon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know how many documents this will be. Maybe I need a truck? Hopefully not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According to what the Defence tells us --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There will be four documents which will in total amount to about 20 pages.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Therefore, you will have 20 or so pages on the outside. But you can already give the witness the first document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document is probably in the possession of the registrar, because I already distributed it. And I have marked my own copy in pencil, so I don't wish to give it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, Mr. Usher, will you pick up the document that you gave to Madam Residovic. So you already have the first document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have one document, sir, and I will be here at 1700, but I don't know where to find the office where I get this. Maybe at the counter or some place. I -- it could be replaced or so. I don't know. Somebody should tell me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bourgon, who is familiar with the building, he will let you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To simplify things, Mr. President, representative of the Victims and Witness Unit will be able to carry the documents to the General to avoid any misunderstanding. So I shall have a meeting with my learned friend from the Prosecution, give him a copy, and at the same time a copy for the Victims and Witness Unit, and they can have this copy sent to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the Victims Unit will contact you and provide you with these documents in due time. If there are no further questions, the hearing is adjourned for today, and we will all resume again tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 6th day of May, 2004, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.53 p.m.,
